cases.title: Private clue discovery
cases.scenario: A Character privately discovers an authored clue through an owning discovery workflow.
cases.expected: One Campaign Clue and one attributable discovery Event are created; only the authorized Player or controller and permitted GM projection receive the clue.

cases.title: Party clue reveal
cases.scenario: An authorized private clue is shared to the party.
cases.expected: Audience preview exposes no hidden extras and one attributable reveal transition expands the permitted audience.

cases.title: Unrevealed clue query
cases.scenario: A Player searches an Investigation containing unrevealed clues.
cases.expected: Unauthorized clues contribute no existence, labels, counts, search hits, diagnostic hints or error distinctions.

cases.title: Hidden connection query
cases.scenario: A Player requests visible semantic connections while a hidden GM edge links two concealed nodes.
cases.expected: The edge and any implied concealed node remain absent from graph, list, outline, table, counts and AI context.

cases.title: Player hypothesis remains theory
cases.scenario: A Player creates a hypothesis from visible clues.
cases.expected: The proposition is stored as a hypothesis with author and version and cannot mutate objective truth or GM solution records.

cases.title: Conflicting hypotheses and open lead
cases.scenario: Players maintain two incompatible hypotheses and create a lead to test them.
cases.expected: Both hypotheses persist with independent support or contradiction links; the lead is explicit and no theory is auto-promoted.

cases.title: False lead without truth corruption
cases.scenario: GM authors a visible clue as an intentional false lead.
cases.expected: The clue may mislead its audience while false-lead metadata stays permission-safe and objective truth remains unchanged.

cases.title: Witness observation and claim
cases.scenario: A witness reports what they believe they saw and GM records a source-reliability assessment.
cases.expected: Observation, claim, witness belief, reliability annotation, authenticity and truth remain separate attributable dimensions.

cases.title: Evidence Asset reference
cases.scenario: A document or physical Item is attached as evidence.
cases.expected: Investigation stores ownerDomain, objectId and objectVersion plus case-local role and notes; ownership and authoritative Item state remain with the source domain.

cases.title: Duplicate discovery delivery
cases.scenario: The same authoritative discovery result is delivered twice.
cases.expected: Idempotency preserves one Campaign Clue discovery and one accepted discovery Event or prior-result receipt.

cases.title: Lost discovery response
cases.scenario: A discovery mutation commits but its response is lost.
cases.expected: Client checks operation status and current version before retry; compatible retry returns the prior result without duplicate state.

cases.title: Stale connection edit
cases.scenario: Two authors edit the same semantic connection from one version.
cases.expected: The stale mutation fails explicitly with current-version and recovery choices; silent last-write-wins is prohibited.

cases.title: Concurrent board layout does not alter semantics
cases.scenario: Two clients arrange the same visible nodes differently while semantic connections remain unchanged.
cases.expected: Presentation conflicts cannot add, remove or reinterpret typed semantic edges; ordered nonvisual relationships remain stable.

cases.title: Disconnect and reconnect
cases.scenario: A Player disconnects during clue activity and reconnects later.
cases.expected: Event-gap recovery is followed by a fresh role-safe projection with no hidden-information replay or stale protected cache.

cases.title: Membership revocation
cases.scenario: Campaign access is revoked after a Player previously viewed protected clues.
cases.expected: Protected caches, search, export, notifications, diagnostics and optional-AI context are invalidated and fresh projections omit revoked content.

cases.title: Pack update preserves live clue snapshot
cases.scenario: A source pack updates a Clue Definition after a Campaign Clue was discovered.
cases.expected: The live Campaign Clue keeps its exact source/version snapshot and history while new template versions remain separately attributable.

cases.title: Pack removal preserves history
cases.scenario: A source pack containing a historical clue becomes unavailable.
cases.expected: Investigation history remains through lawful snapshot or tombstone representation and source removal does not erase discoveries, hypotheses or conclusions.

cases.title: Player export is authorization filtered
cases.scenario: A Player exports their visible Investigation projection through the universal export surface.
cases.expected: Only authorized projections and permitted provenance are exported; hidden truth, clues, sources, edges and counts remain absent.

cases.title: Diagnostic bundle uses identical privacy filter
cases.scenario: A support diagnostic bundle is produced for a Player-facing Investigation problem.
cases.expected: The same authorization and redaction rules apply; hidden truth or object existence cannot leak through diagnostics.

cases.title: Optional AI organization remains draft
cases.scenario: Optional AI organizes visible clues and proposes a connection and theory label.
cases.expected: Only authorized context is supplied; generated output remains proposal-only until explicit authorized acceptance with provenance.

cases.title: AI request for hidden truth denied
cases.scenario: A Player-context AI request attempts to inspect GM truth or concealed solution material.
cases.expected: Authorization denies protected truth without confirming hidden content existence, counts or shape.

cases.title: Keyboard semantic connection creation
cases.scenario: A keyboard-only user creates a supports connection through ordered node selectors and a form.
cases.expected: Full connection creation is possible without dragging; predicate, source, target, rationale, visibility and version are preserved.

cases.title: Screen-reader board review
cases.scenario: A screen-reader user reviews the clue board through ordered textual projections.
cases.expected: Nodes and typed predicates convey the same required meaning as the graph and focus order does not depend on canvas coordinates.

cases.title: GM resolution preserves hypothesis history
cases.scenario: GM records an authorized conclusion after Players developed several theories.
cases.expected: Conclusion is attributable and durable while prior Player hypotheses, discoveries and rejected alternatives remain in history.

cases.title: Dr. Wen dossier projection integrity
cases.scenario: The source-backed The Vanishing of Dr. Wen dossier is represented as one governed Investigation with separate Player-facing case material and GM solution material.
cases.expected: The contract can represent case identity, clues and source provenance while GM truth/solution stays separately authorized; no unprovided Dr. Wen content is invented by the fixture.

cases.title: Important revelation single-route warning
cases.scenario: An author marks an important required revelation with only one explicit discovery route.
cases.expected: The diagnostic reports reachability plus a single-point and redundancy warning; it does not declare the mystery invalid or invent another clue.

cases.title: Important revelation has two independent routes
cases.scenario: An important required revelation has two distinct explicit routes that do not collapse through duplicate-of links.
cases.expected: The source-grounded at-least-two redundancy warning condition is satisfied while the diagnostic makes no claim that overall mystery quality or success is guaranteed.

cases.title: Circular revelation dependency
cases.scenario: Required revelation A requires B and B requires A with no external entry route.
cases.expected: Deterministic diagnostics report the circular unreachable dependency and do not auto-repair, reveal or resolve either revelation.

cases.title: False lead with authored recovery route
cases.scenario: A deliberate false lead can consume attention, but an explicit later clue or recovery route returns investigators to a required revelation.
cases.expected: The false lead remains attributable, recovery provenance is explicit and the diagnostic reports a recovery path without calling the false lead objectively fair or unfair.

cases.title: Misleading material is sole required route
cases.scenario: Every explicit route to a required revelation depends solely on material designated false, corrupted or forged and no correction route exists.
cases.expected: The diagnostic reports the authored risk deterministically; it does not decide truth, delete the misleading material or impose a universal fairness threshold.

cases.title: Timeline alibi contradiction review
cases.scenario: A witness alibi places them at one location while an attributable event record places the subject elsewhere during an overlapping time window.
cases.expected: A temporal contradiction may be authored or diagnosed for review, but neither side becomes true or false automatically and both source records remain intact.

cases.title: Source-quality dimensions remain independent
cases.scenario: A reliable witness sincerely repeats content from a forged document.
cases.expected: Witness belief/reliability and document authenticity are represented independently; confidence/relevance annotations do not become truth probability.

cases.title: Research success cannot bypass reveal permission
cases.scenario: A successful Research or Knowledge result points toward information that remains GM-only under current reveal policy.
cases.expected: The owning resolution result is retained, but PPIA-09 exposes only the authorized discovery or analysis projection and does not reveal protected truth automatically.

cases.title: Hidden world timeline fact does not leak
cases.scenario: A case timeline references a PPIA-12 chronology fact that is not Player-known.
cases.expected: GM authoring may retain the reference while Player timeline, counts, alibi hints and diagnostics omit the protected fact until authorized knowledge projection exists.

cases.title: Dynamic extra clue retains provenance
cases.scenario: The GM introduces an extra clue after an authored stall condition is met.
cases.expected: The clue records author, trigger or delivery reason, source, audience, Event evidence and version so later review distinguishes adaptive recovery from baseline clue placement.

cases.title: Cross-case correlation creates a lead, not truth
cases.scenario: Authorized historical records from another Investigation share a source or subject with the current case.
cases.expected: A typed correlation and follow-up lead may be authored with provenance, but cross-case similarity does not automatically establish objective truth or reveal hidden material.
